image_description: A close-up, high-resolution portrait of a male mallard duck (drake) resting with its head tucked back onto its shoulder. The image highlights the iridescent green head, yellow bill, and the transition to brown chest and grey/white body feathers. The background is a smooth, out-of-focus grey-blue.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows dense, layered feathering typical of waterproof plumage. The curvature suggests a compact, streamlined shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head displays the characteristic iridescent green sheen of a breeding mallard drake. The chest is chestnut/brown, transitioning to lighter feathers, which aligns with mallard patterning.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely occluded by the body and the angle of the shot; they are not visible in the frame.
The wings are folded against the body and largely obscured by the head and neck position; their full shape and pointedness cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the frame or completely occluded by the body's curvature and cropping.
